notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 04/03/2025
Patient: Cecil Jacobs, 83-year-old male

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 04/03/2025. The study evaluated sleep architecture and respiratory events throughout the night. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 36.4 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 16% of all events. Oxygen saturation showed intermittent drops corresponding to apneic episodes, with a lowest saturation of 82%. Sleep stages were within expected ranges for age, with normal REM and non-REM distribution. No significant periodic limb movements were noted. These findings indicate moderate to severe sleep apnea with a significant central component. Further clinical correlation and treatment planning are advised.

Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 08/10/2026
Patient: Cecil Jacobs, 84-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Mr. Jacobs is an 84-year-old male referred for assessment of sleep apnea management. He has a history of obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed several years ago.

Physical Examination:
BMI 31.6 kg/m2.

Sleep Study and Treatment:
CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 1.3 hours per night on 21% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Plan:
Given the documented CPAP intolerance, alternative therapies for sleep apnea will be considered. Options include oral appliance therapy and positional therapy. Patient education and follow-up will be arranged to monitor symptoms and treatment adherence.

Summary:
Mr. Jacobs has obesity with BMI 31.6 kg/m2 and documented CPAP intolerance despite efforts to optimize therapy. Shared decision-making supports exploring other treatment modalities to improve sleep quality and reduce apnea events.
